member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Aggregates.ApplyMethodResolver
member.summary: The single shared discovery and resolution engine for the runtime public void Apply(TEvent) convention. Both the aggregate/rehydrate path (DomainProcessorStateRehydrator, ) and the projection path () resolve through this type, so the two former copy-pasted resolvers cannot drift apart again.

remarks.para: Persisters record Type.FullName, so every event type is registered under both its full name and its short name. Resolution order is: exact full-name key, then exact short-name key, then a boundary-anchored suffix scan where the longest anchored candidate wins.

A candidate key k matches a stored name n only when n == k or n ends with "." + k or "+" + k. The + boundary is how renders nested types. Unanchored matching (the previous behaviour) let Billing.SubOrderCreated bind Apply(OrderCreated).

A key claimed by more than one event type is never resolved by picking one: it is recorded as ambiguous and reported at resolution time with . Reporting at resolution rather than registration keeps an aggregate whose events collide only by short name working whenever those events are addressed by their full names.

The suffix scan reads from a dedicated key map that unions the full-name and short-name aliases. Selecting one map over the other would hide a real collision: a global-namespace event type registers key K as its full name while a namespaced Ns.K registers the same key as its short name, and a stored X.K anchors on both.

member.name: M:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Aggregates.ApplyMethodResolver.NormalizeTypeName(System.String)
member.summary: Removes assembly qualification from a CLR type name at every bracket level, so "Ns.Type, Asm, Version=1.0.0.0" becomes "Ns.Type" and "Ns.Outer`1[[Ns.Arg, Asm, Version=1.0.0.0]]" becomes "Ns.Outer`1[[Ns.Arg]]".
member.remarks: Splitting on the first comma (the previous behaviour) truncated a constructed generic mid-argument, producing a fragment such as "Ns.Outer`1[[Ns.Arg" that could then anchor a suffix match against Apply(Arg) — a silent wrong bind. Because both the registered key and the stored name pass through this same function, matching stays consistent even for shapes it normalizes only partially.

member.remarks: Instances are published from a process-wide static cache and read concurrently, so every member is a genuinely immutable type ( / ) rather than a mutable collection behind a read-only-looking property.

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Configuration.EventStoreDomainOptions
member.summary: Per-domain configuration options for event store resource naming. Used in the five-layer cascading configuration system where each layer can override individual properties. A null value means "not set at this layer — use value from previous layer."

remarks.para:
The cascade resolution applies layers in priority order (lowest to highest):
Layer 1 — Convention defaults (from NamingConventionEngine)
Layer 2 — Global code options (from EventStoreOptions)
Layer 3 — Domain self-config (OnConfiguring() override)
Layer 4 — External config (appsettings.json)
Layer 5 — Explicit override (ConfigureDomain() callback)

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Gateway.EventStoreGatewayClient
member.summary: HTTP implementation of .
Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.remarks:
DEC6: this constructor mutates on the supplied . Because instances are commonly shared across consumers, the buffer cap applies to ALL endpoints invoked via the same client. Configure a typed client per gateway when other endpoints (e.g., large query responses) need a higher cap.
P16-8P (pass-8): the buffer cap is now applied min-only — the constructor reduces the cap when the option is smaller than the caller-configured existing value, but it never raises a lower caller cap. This restores the pre-DEC6-7P behavior and prevents silent behavior change when callers pre-size HttpClient.MaxResponseContentBufferSize for narrow workloads.
P22-7P (pass-7 MEDIUM): when multiple gateway clients are constructed concurrently against the same shared with different values, the min-only assignment is still a race (last-writer-wins on the equal-or-smaller branch). The recommended deployment pattern is one typed client per gateway via named DI options (services.AddHttpClient<EventStoreGatewayClient>(...)), giving each gateway its own HttpClient instance. The shared-HttpClient pattern is supported for compatibility but not optimal under multi-tenant DI configuration.

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Handlers.LegacyCommandReplayInput
member.summary: Bounds and clears private contract-envelope copies used by legacy command reconstruction.
member.remarks: Nested envelope sequences share one count, readable-payload and live-array admission budget. This local owner grants no authenticated source authority or bound on typed state/event graphs. JSON documents and base64 buffers are admitted before private materialization. Original transport parsing and application converter/typed graph allocations remain unqualified. Typed snapshots are detached only when their owner supplies an explicit capture declaration. Optional folded capture additionally debits its qualified event-buffer and detached-graph reservations before copying envelopes or parsing retained JSON token tables. Those representations cannot use the unrelated legacy ceiling to expand capture workspace. Decoded domain graphs and strings still require the owner's qualified serializer and callback bounds; this ledger does not measure or confine undeclared callback allocations.

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Projections.IReadModelBatchStore
member.summary: Opt-in, same-store coordinated batch capability for persisted read models.

remarks.para: This is an additive companion to : it lets a projection author persist several heterogeneous typed writes and deletes (for example a detail model and its index entry) as one coordinated unit within a single configured DAPR state-store component, so a reader never observes an updated detail model paired with a missing or stale index entry.

The execution is immediate and asynchronous: one immutable in, one structured out. There is no mutable builder, buffered flush, or fire-and-forget work. Expected concurrency and durable-recovery outcomes are reported through the result status; only validation, programming, and configuration errors throw.
The same concrete instance also implements ; the platform registers one singleton behind both interfaces (see AddEventStoreReadModelStore).

member.summary: Executes a coordinated read-model batch against its configured store component.
member.param: The immutable batch manifest (scope, ordered operations, concurrency policy).

A cancellation token. Cancellation requested before any state access throws ; cancellation observed after a request may have reached the store triggers bounded durable reconciliation rather than being treated as a rollback.
member.returns: A structured distinguishing completed success, idempotent already-completed success, conflict, incomplete, and indeterminate outcomes.

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Projections.IReadModelFreshness
member.summary: Optional metadata a persisted read model can expose so that consumers can classify its freshness from a real persisted projection timestamp and/or version, instead of inferring it from transport signals (ETags, degraded flags) or hand-rolling a per-domain timestamp field.

remarks.para: A read model implements this interface to advertise when the projection that produced it was last updated. The value is persisted as part of the read model itself (it is set by the projection on every write and round-trips through ), so it survives reads and reflects the true last-projected instant rather than the moment a gateway served a response.
The interface is purely additive: existing read models that do not implement it keep working, and freshness classification simply returns for them (see ).

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Projections.IReadModelStore
member.summary: Persisted read-model store for domain modules that maintain incrementally-updated, multi-key read models in a DAPR state store.

remarks.para: This is the platform generalization of the per-domain projection state stores domain modules previously hand-wrote (e.g. DaprTenantProjectionStateStore). It is a thin wrapper over the DAPR state-store API exposing only what a persisted read model needs: ETag-aware reads and optimistic-concurrency writes. The higher-level reload-and-merge retry loop lives in , which is built on top of this interface so it can be unit-tested against an in-memory store without a DAPR sidecar.

Multi-key/index read models are supported by simply addressing different key values: a per-aggregate read model uses a key derived from the aggregate identity, while a cross-aggregate index uses a single fixed key whose value is merged on every write via .

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Projections.ProjectionChangedDetail
member.summary:
Opaque, metadata-only detail for a projection-changed broadcast.
Values in are treated as metadata by the framework and MUST NOT carry authoritative content (no response text, chunks, prompts, or domain payloads). Domain meaning lives in the consuming application; the framework stays content-agnostic so the metadata-only floor is enforceable at the framework boundary.
, when present, narrows the SignalR group below tenant level (for example, a conversation id), producing the group name {ProjectionType}:{TenantId}:{GroupScope}. When or empty, the broadcast targets the tenant-wide group {ProjectionType}:{TenantId}.
member.param: Optional sub-tenant group scope (for example, a conversation id). Null or empty targets the tenant-wide group; a non-empty value targets the scoped group.

Opaque, bounded metadata key/value pairs. Never authoritative content. Bounds (key count and compact JSON UTF-8 size, including punctuation and escaping) are enforced by the broadcaster at the framework boundary. The contract ceilings are 16 entries and 2,048 bytes.

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Projections.ReadModelBatchCanonicalJson
member.summary: Deterministic, culture-invariant JSON canonicalization used for fingerprinting and for the bytes persisted by coordinated batches. Object properties are emitted in ordinal name order so the output is independent of reflection/serializer property ordering.
member.remarks: The serializer options are intentionally fixed to (the DAPR default) rather than a consumer-supplied DaprClient.JsonSerializerOptions: the canonical bytes are the versioned fingerprint material, so they must be stable across deployments and independent of runtime configuration (changing them is a versioned contract change validated by a golden-vector test). Coordinated batch writes therefore require the store's effective DAPR JSON options to remain the Web defaults; a consumer that customizes DaprClient.JsonSerializerOptions (custom converters, naming policy) must not use the batch seam, because the single-key read path (DaprReadModelStore.GetAsync) deserializes with those custom options and batch-written values would not round-trip. A registration guard test pins the default assumption.

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Projections.ReadModelBatchFingerprint
member.summary: Computes the versioned canonical fingerprint that binds a batch identity to its exact operations.
member.remarks: The fingerprint material includes, for every operation in ordinal order: the ordinal, logical key, write/delete kind, stable value type identity, concurrency mode and expected ETag, and the canonical DAPR-compatible JSON value bytes. A configured operation TTL participates as rounded-up whole seconds; an omitted TTL adds no field, preserving the original v1 golden vector. The scope components participate as well. The algorithm is frozen at v1 and covered by golden-vector tests; changing it is a versioned contract change. Deadline-bearing batches explicitly select v2 and bind UTC ticks; v1 bytes stay unchanged.

member.summary: A single immutable operation within a coordinated read-model batch.
member.remarks: Write operations serialize their value once, at construction, into immutable canonical UTF-8 JSON bytes. member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Projections.ReadModelBatchProtocol
member.summary: The shared coordinated-batch protocol engine. A fresh instance is created per ExecuteAsync call and runs identically over the DAPR adapter and the in-memory fake, so both expose equivalent observable outcomes. It implements both the transaction-qualified and marker-gated resumable profiles, bounded same-identity reconciliation after ambiguous dispatch, pre-commit compensation, and post-commit compaction, plus the shared read-visibility resolution used by GetAsync.

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Projections.ReadModelBatchResult
member.summary: The structured outcome of a coordinated read-model batch execution.
member.remarks: The status enum alone cannot express identity-versus-optimistic conflicts or the recovery reason without lossy interpretation, so those travel as explicit members. Expected concurrency and durable-recovery outcomes are reported here; only validation, programming, and configuration errors throw. Envelope/marker compaction is completed and verified before a result is returned, so there is no separate cleanup-pending completion state in this story; if a bounded asynchronous cleanup horizon is introduced later (Story 1.13), it must reintroduce that member as a versioned contract change.
member.param: The versioned canonical fingerprint of the batch that was evaluated.

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Projections.ReadModelBatchScope
member.summary: Stable identity scope for a coordinated read-model batch.
member.remarks: The scope binds a batch to a single store component and a single logical projection delivery. Its components are hashed into an opaque, collision-resistant marker namespace so no raw tenant data or payload content ever appears in a marker key. is a stable, caller-supplied message/ULID identity — never a value generated fresh per retry — and is validated only as a non-whitespace token (consistent with the platform's aggregate-identity rules); it is never parsed with Guid.TryParse.
member.param: The DAPR state-store component name. All operations target this one store.
The aggregate identifier the projection delivery is for.

member.summary: Generic, threshold-based freshness classification for a persisted read model, derived from a real persisted projection timestamp via .

remarks.para: This is the platform generalization of the per-domain freshness enums domain modules previously hand-wrote (e.g. TenantFreshnessState). It lets consumers compute "aging"/"stale" states generically from a single persisted projection timestamp instead of each domain re-deriving the thresholds. member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Projections.ReadModelWritePolicy
member.summary: Optimistic-concurrency, merge-on-write helpers for persisted read models built on .

remarks.para: This is the platform generalization of the per-domain projection write policies domain modules previously hand-wrote (e.g. TenantProjectionWritePolicy). Every write follows the same reload-and-merge contract: read the current value (and ETag), produce the next value from it, and attempt a first-write-wins save. On an ETag conflict the loaded value is stale, so the loop re-reads and re-applies up to times before failing.

The transform passed to MUST be idempotent with respect to the loaded value: it may run more than once (on each retry) and, for event-replay read models, the same events may be re-applied to an already-updated value. Callers must ensure re-applying does not duplicate list entries, double-count, or otherwise diverge from a from-scratch rebuild.

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Queries.IQueryCursorCodec
member.summary: Encodes and validates protected, opaque pagination cursors for domain queries.

remarks.para: This is the platform generalization of the per-domain cursor codecs domain modules previously hand-wrote (e.g. TenantQueryCursorCodec). A cursor protects a logical pagination position together with the queryType and scope it was issued for, so a cursor minted for one query/scope can never be replayed against another. The position is opaque to clients and tamper-evident: it is sealed with ASP.NET Core Data Protection.

Domains supply only the scope fields — compose a stable, collision-safe scope string with and pass it to /. Cross-domain cryptographic isolation comes from the codec's Data Protection purpose, configured at registration time (see AddEventStoreQueryCursorCodec).

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Queries.QueryCursorScope
member.summary: Builds a stable, collision-safe scope string for use with .

remarks.para: A cursor scope binds a cursor to the exact endpoint/filter set it was issued for, so a cursor minted for one caller's view cannot be replayed against another's. Domains supply only the scope fields (key/value pairs); this builder produces the canonical string.

The format uses '|' as the segment separator and ':' as the key/value separator. Both characters (and the escape character '\') are escaped inside caller-supplied values so an attacker-controlled identifier cannot collide with another scope by injecting a separator. Keys are caller-controlled literals and are written verbatim. The resulting string is deterministic for a given ordered set of fields.

member.name: T:Hexalith.EventStore.Client.Reminders.IReminderIntentSource
member.summary: Domain-implemented source of durable reminder intents. EventStore owns registration, callbacks, and reconciliation; the domain module owns what its committed events mean.
member.remarks:
Both members must be deterministic and clock-free. EventStore calls them inside the target's serialized reminder turn, both when converging and again before submitting a callback, so the stream, never a persisted index or callback payload, decides which intents are current. An instance can live as long as a reminder actor activation, so it must read the stream on every call rather than cache it.
Stop reporting an intent once its target has handled the submitted command; otherwise every convergence resubmits it and replays the receipt.
Keep (source domain, source aggregate, source sequence, kind, target) unique among current intents. Intents that share it share one effect identity and are quarantined as effect-collision. Two current intents with different evidence under one name are recorded as witness-collision even when that name also shares an effect identity. Convergence records a changed stored witness whose name participates in an effect collision as effect-collision; callback admission records its changed evidence as witness-collision.
Retain the source coordinates when retrying the same logical submission. For the same kind and target, a distinct logical submission needs distinct committed source-event coordinates: changing only the due instant or schedule revision retains the previous effect identity and replays its receipt or conflicts with changed command semantics.
Distinct current witnesses must derive distinct reminder names. The name binds the tenant, target aggregate, kind, due instant, and schedule revision. Persist a new schedule revision when the source coordinates, payload type, or payload change; different evidence under the same name is quarantined as witness-collision.
Keep aggregate identifiers unique across every domain that shares one reminder actor type: the AD-11 actor tuple omits the domain, so a second domain with the same aggregate identifier is quarantined as actor-collision.

member.returns: The current intents. An empty list means the stream holds none. A null result is not an empty stream and must not be used to cancel stored reminders.
